page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Running head at top with the page number 354 beside it. Heading "ARTICVLVS QVARTVS." with subtitle "De Meteoris Aëreis.", then a paragraph 1, a heading "D.E. IRIDE.", paragraphs 2 to 4 in one column, and at the foot the catchword "5. Cæte-".

main_text.l: ARTICULUS QUARTUS.
De Meteoris Aëreis.
1. Meteora aërea vulgò ponuntur ista, Iris, ventus, vorago, hiatus,
halo, parclius[?], & parasclene[?].
D.E. IRIDE.
2. Iris est arcus multicolor in nube rorida, concava, & opaca, ex
radiorum solarium reflexione apparens; quæ definitio compre-
hendit causam efficientem & materialem Iridis. Causa enim efficiens Iri-
dis est Sol vibrans radios in nubem: Causa vero materialis est nubes ror-
ida recipiens solares radios. Fit autem Iris vulgò, quando Sol emittit
radios in nubem roridam & diaphanam in parte inferiori, & opacam in
parte superiori; ex eo enim quòd nubes sit ita disposita fit ut recipiat lu-
cem Solis, quam reflectit ad nos ob quandam opacitatem, quæ radiis so-
laribus non penetratur.
3. Lux intercepta intra nubem nobis repræsentat diversos colores: Cum
enim nubes in suprema parte sit crassior, eâ parte colorem purpureum
& rubrum refert; nam lumen permixtum exhalationi nigræ & densæ re-
fert rubrum colorem, ut patet in carbone accenso, & aliis similibus;
medius color nobis apparet viridis, eò quòd nubes in medio rarior sit,
quàm in summo, ultimus verò color apparet cæruleus, quia nubes in
inferiori parte rarior est quàm in medio & summo: Alii addunt colo-
rem flavum, & alios minùs præcipuos. Scaliger existimavit nubem con-
stare ex omnium elementorum particulis, & supremas excipientes lu-
cem rutilare tanquam igneas, sequentes flavescere tanquam aëreas, ter-
tias virescere tanquam aqueas, extremas fieri cæruleas & nigricantes
tanquam terreas.
4. Figura Iridis est circularis aut in arcum; quia radii Solis à corpo-
re Solis tanquam à centro aut quasi centro diffunduntur æqualiter per li-
neam rectam; hoc enim habent omnia corpora luminosa, ut ab unoquo-
que sui puncto emittant radios per lineas rectas æqualiter; ex quo sequi-
tur, ut radii omnes simul qui procedunt à corpore luminoso semper desinant
in circulum aut semicirculum; non quòd radii singuli efficiant cir-
culum aut semicirculum, cum singuli terminentur puncto, sed quòd linea quæ ducitur ab extremis punctis
lineatum sit semper circularis aut in arcum.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "parclius" and "parasclene" in paragraph 1 are read with [?] because the small print makes the letters e/c and the second vowel unclear. The large initial M of "Meteora" and the initial I of "Iris" are taken as the first letter of the word. Dotted spaced capitals in the running head and "D.E. IRIDE." are normalised to plain capitals and spacing. The catchword "5. Cæte-" is kept as printed and ends with a hyphen. The digitiser's mark at the bottom right is omitted. The printed "lineatum" in paragraph 4 is left as printed.
